basis: Skeletal growth abnormalities define syndrome; developmental and speech delay occur in 30–79%. Feeding difficulty and fasting hypoglycemia alone do not establish organ damage.
Adenoma of nipple ducts is a breast neoplasm; breast has no axis.
Hereditary giant neutrophils constitute a blood-cell abnormality; sparse information provides no evidence of other organ involvement.
Defined by structural or functional impairment of arteries; additional organ injury is subtype-dependent.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease and bronchiectasis; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 8/12 patients.
Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder; extracutaneous damage is not established across most subtypes.
Congenital generalized hair overgrowth defines disease; dental anomalies are described without evidence that damaging abnormalities reach 30%.
Ischemic inflammation damages the colon; reduced perfusion does not necessarily establish intrinsic vessel disease or immune-mediated inflammation.
Psychiatric disorder of appearance-related preoccupation without defining damage to an organ axis.
Malignant neoplasm occupying the rectum; lymphoma is only one subtype, and metastatic organ damage is not universal.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; cystic renal dysplasia, hydrocephalus and intestinal malrotation each occur in 1/2 reported patients; estimates derive from a tiny series.
Specific neurodevelopmental learning disorder affecting numerical processing.
Bone fragility defines disease; progressive hearing loss affects roughly 30–50% over adulthood. Blue sclerae are non-damaging; dentinogenesis imperfecta is under 30%.
EBV-associated B-cell lymphoproliferation typically occupies lungs; destructive skin lesions occur in ~30–50%. CNS disease is borderline at ~20–30% and excluded under the cap.
Embryonal malignant tumor arising in the supratentorial central nervous system.
Metabolic myopathy, acidosis and sensorineural deafness define syndrome; seizures, spasticity and dystonia occur in 1/1 annotated patient; evidence is limited.
Glycosylation defect with immunodeficiency; neurodevelopmental injury in 1/1 and anemia in 2/2. Cap excludes vasculitis and arthritis, each 1/1; liver findings are nonspecific.
Intellectual disability and cranial skeletal abnormalities define syndrome. Reported bradycardia alone does not establish lasting cardiac damage.
Lipoic acid biosynthesis defect with defining encephalopathy; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy reported in 1/1 annotated patient. Respiratory insufficiency alone does not show lung damage.
Osteonecrosis directly destroys the femoral head; avascularity alone does not establish a separate intrinsic vascular disorder.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with global developmental delay in 17/17; individual extracerebral abnormalities occur below 30%.
Phosphate metabolism and electrolyte disorder; renal disease may cause it but is not intrinsic to the concept.
Autoimmune injury of peripheral nerves or neuromuscular junction; other organ involvement is subtype-dependent.
Intestinal infection produces toxin that blocks neuromuscular and autonomic transmission; ocular, bowel and respiratory manifestations chiefly reflect neural dysfunction.
Meningioma occupying the periocular region; this location does not itself establish intracranial meningeal involvement.
